title: Sarasbaug Siddhivinayak (Talyatla Ganpati)
text:
Sarasbaug Siddhivinayak (Talyatla Ganpati) (सारसबाग सिद्धिविनायक (तळ्यातला गणपती)) — Not Manacha, located in Sarasbaug, Pune, established 18th century (Peshwa era).

History: Sarasbaug Ganpati, also called Talyatla Ganpati ('Ganpati of the lake'), was built during the Peshwa era and houses Shree Siddhivinayak, the wish-fulfilling form of Ganesha. Set within the 25-acre Sarasbaug complex — originally an artificial lake — the temple sees over 10,000 devotees on an average day, rising to 80,000 on Ganesh Chaturthi. It is a peaceful, scenic alternative to Dagdusheth for a quieter morning darshan, administered by the Peshwa Trust.

Idol/Deity: Traditional Siddhivinayak idol within a garden setting — peaceful, less crowded than the peth mandals.

Temple/Mandir address: Sarasbaug, Near Swargate, Pune 411037. Festival pandal address: Permanent temple — darshan at the temple itself. Maps link: https://goo.gl/maps/sarasbaug. Coordinates: 18.5009, 73.853.

Aarti timings — Morning: 6:00 AM; Evening: 8:00 PM.

Special events during the 10 days: Special aarti during Ganesh Chaturthi; garden illuminated during festival; relatively peaceful compared to peth mandals.

Note: Confirm 2026 timings; good to mention as quieter darshan option in app
